newsitem.title: UK: Quiet NWE fuel oil markets end week mixed.
newsitem.headline: Quiet NWE fuel oil markets end week mixed.

text.p: European fuel oil markets ended the week mixed on Friday, with barges firming on bunker demand and low sulphur pressured on the quiet physical market by poorer swaps. A 3,000 tonne barge of high sulphur fuel oil traded at $80.25 a tonne early in the day in the ARA area, but at least three other deals were reported done later at $83, $83.25 and $83.50.

The highest reported figure compared with a high of $83 on Thursday. The seller of the first cargo was said to be keen to sell material early in the day, and later raised his offer price to $82.50 a tonne for RMG material. Traders said the high sulphur cargo market was quietly talked a little firmer at about the $80 per tonne cif on Friday as not too many sellers were seen on the market. "There's not a huge number of people offering cargoes, but then there's not a huge number wanting to buy either," the trader said. Traders said that while Russian cracked material was not overly pressuring the European market at present, they expressed fears that it could build up again. "If there is a build-up of cracked material then that might start to put pressure on the (high sulphur) market again," one trader said. Low sulphur fuel oil was talked a little weaker further in the day at $92/$94 a tonne fob, or $2 down on Thursday's levels, with pressure coming from poorer swaps, traders said.
